content: Hydroxyzine is a medication prescribed to alleviate itching caused by allergies. It is also used to manage nausea and vomiting associated with various conditions, including motion sickness. Additionally, it is prescribed for anxiety and to address symptoms related to alcohol withdrawal. In some cases, it may be used for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further details. Hydroxyzine is available in capsules, tablets, syrup, and suspension forms, all of which are taken orally. It is typically taken three or four times a day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take hydroxyzine exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed. If you are using the suspension form (Vistaril), shake the bottle well before each use to ensure the medication is evenly mixed. Do not administer this medication to children under 12 years of age unless specifically directed by a doctor. Before taking hydroxyzine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to hydroxyzine or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially antihistamines, medications for colds, allergies, or hay fever, medications for depression or seizures, muscle relaxants, narcotics (pain medications), sedatives, sleeping pills, tranquilizers, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had asthma, glaucoma, ulcers, difficulty urinating (due to an enlarged prostate gland), heart disease, liver disease, high blood pressure, seizures, or an overactive thyroid gland. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking hydroxyzine, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking hydroxyzine. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can enhance the drowsiness caused by this medication, so it is advisable to avoid alcohol while taking hydroxyzine. If you miss a dose of hydroxyzine, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Hydroxyzine may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms and they are severe or persistent: dry mouth, nose, or throat; upset stomach; drowsiness; dizziness; chest congestion; headache; or skin redness. If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: difficulty breathing, muscle weakness, or increased anxiety. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store hydroxyzine in the container it came in, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor while taking this medication. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
